clue.text: No longer offer accompanying attraction

parts.note: to go with someone is to accompany them
a draw is something that pulls in crowds, an attraction

explanation.surface: A venue drops the extra event it had been promising alongside the main show.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw an offer is to take it back so that it no longer stands.

clue.text: The Ship -bar in which a girl turns up

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces sit inside the bar just named

parts.note: an inn is a bar, a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: In a pub called The Ship, a young woman suddenly appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' works because this is a down clue, so the reversed letters read upwards. 'The' looks like part of a pub name but is only surface dressing, a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant sailing vessel trading with India.

clue.text: Old English invading Scottish island? Nonsense

indicators.note: invading says the first piece pushes its way inside the island

parts.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands, off the north of Scotland

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon raid on a Hebridean isle is dismissed as fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooey is informal slang for silly talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Soldiers in first quarter of regiment?

definitions.text: Soldiers in first quarter of regiment?

parts.words: Soldiers in first quarter of regiment?
parts.note: the first two of the eight letters of 'regiment' are R and E, the abbreviation for a corps of army engineers

explanation.surface: Which troops are found at the front of a regiment?
explanation.walkthrough: A quarter of the word REGIMENT is its first two letters, RE, and RE is the usual abbreviation for this corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The corps of military engineers in the British Army is a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Western liturgy exalted in report

parts.note: a rite is a form of liturgy, a set ceremony of worship
exalted means raised up

explanation.surface: A church service in the Western tradition is praised in a press account.
explanation.definitionFit: A write-up is a published account or review of something.

clue.text: Moves fast like a yacht, not getting caught in foam

indicators.note: not getting says the letter for caught is left out

parts.note: a yacht before the wind scuds, racing along
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A racing yacht dodges capture amid the spray of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Suds are the froth or lather on soapy water.

clue.text: Witness cops treat badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of these two words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who saw the incident describes police treating a suspect roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker, someone who sees an event happen.

clue.text: Tyrant drank too much, belting son on rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the whole build reads from bottom to top
belting means putting a belt round, so the drinking word encloses the letter for son

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so toped means drank too much

explanation.surface: A drunken dictator beats his own son as he gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belting' puts S inside TOPED to make TOPSED, and 'rising' turns that upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly.

clue.text: Four or equivalent?

explanation.surface: A number, or something matching it?
explanation.walkthrough: On a standard die opposite faces add up to seven, so the face showing four sits opposite three.
explanation.definitionFit: Four lies across a die from three; and a counterpart doing the same job in another organisation is someone's equivalent.

clue.text: I'd cold, swallowing nothing — stupid behaviour

parts.note: I'd gives its letters without the apostrophe

indicators.note: swallowing says the word for cold takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: icy means very cold
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with a chill who will not eat is behaving foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is extreme foolishness, the conduct of an idiot.

clue.text: Reporter's comment is to look good

explanation.surface: A journalist remarks that it is all about appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: A reporter might say 'I'm press', which run together spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist could announce 'I'm press'; and to make a favourable mark on people is to look good to them.

clue.text: A shade negative and depressed about volume

indicators.note: about says the word for negative wraps round the next letter

parts.note: nay is a negative answer, no
feeling blue means feeling depressed

explanation.surface: A downbeat colour sits gloomily around a loud volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy blue is a dark blue colour, a shade.

clue.text: Excel — getting dismissed by spinner?

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket batter shines until bowled out by a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'spinner' is a slow bowler who spins the ball, but here it is the spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To outtop someone is to outdo them, to surpass or excel.

clue.text: Student in accepting drug's brought in fashionable topic

indicators.note: in says the letter for student goes inside the word for accepting

parts.note: taking means accepting, as in taking an offer
L, from the learner plate, stands for student

indicators.note: brought in says the drug word takes the fashionable word into its middle

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis; the 's means has
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A student caught with drugs becomes the subject everyone discusses.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking point is a subject for discussion.

clue.text: Gives up hooker? That's a boost

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up, so kicks means gives up
tart is a slang word for a prostitute, as is hooker

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a rugby hooker and finds it energising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' suggests the rugby position, but it is slang for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is a sudden impetus that gets something going, a boost.

clue.text: Bear unhappily in discomfort-Pooh's self-description?

indicators.note: in says the rearranged bear goes inside the word for discomfort

parts.note: pain means discomfort

indicators.note: unhappily says the letters of bear end up in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A sad bear in some pain sums himself up as Winnie-the-Pooh does.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie-the-Pooh calls himself 'a Bear of Very Little Brain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-brain is a stupid person, and Pooh describes himself as having very little brain.

clue.text: Dog trainer upset when grabbed by announcer

indicators.note: grabbed by says the reordered trainer is held inside the announcer word

parts.note: a town crier makes public announcements

indicators.note: upset says the letters of trainer are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dog trainer is upset when seized by a public announcer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cairn terrier is a small Scottish breed of dog.

clue.text: Such as close relatives live in home

indicators.note: in says the word for live sits inside the word for home

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
to be is to exist or live, so are means live

explanation.surface: Close family members all live together under one roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls up the phrase 'nearest and dearest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Close relatives are described as one's nearest and dearest.

clue.text: Pass recess with the Spanish

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
an apse is a vaulted recess in a church

explanation.surface: A church alcove is visited along with some Spaniards.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or go by; it elapses.

clue.text: East Anglian city and its description in Parisian palace

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, East Anglia
Ely is a see, the seat of a bishop, so see describes it

explanation.surface: A Cambridgeshire cathedral city and its description in a French palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president.

clue.text: A friend curtailed regular behaviour in Arab city

parts.note: bud, short for buddy, means friend

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a habit is a regular pattern of behaviour

explanation.surface: A friend's routine is cut short while staying in a Gulf city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' looks as if it belongs to 'friend' but cuts the final T from HABIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Bother a chap

explanation.surface: Pester a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or pester; and Harry is a man's name, so a chap.

clue.text: Plain song that is behind priest

indicators.note: behind says the song and the that-is pieces follow the priest letter

parts.note: priest gives PR
an air is a tune or song
ie, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A simple hymn follows the clergyman down the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide, flat grassland, a plain.

clue.text: Pub worker to exclude lots? Not quite

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them

indicators.note: not quite says the word for lots loses its final letter

parts.note: many means lots

explanation.surface: A publican wants to throw out a crowd, but stops short.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman serves drinks behind the bar of a pub.

clue.text: Relaxation requires this, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some relaxation is said to be needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest is repose, a break from activity.

clue.text: Waiting's onerous, occupying half year? On the contrary

indicators.note: occupying would put the onerous word inside the year piece
on the contrary flips the container, so the year piece goes inside instead

parts.note: trying means onerous, hard to bear

indicators.note: half of the four-letter year takes its second pair of letters

explanation.surface: Waiting around is a burden, filling half the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' read straight would put the onerous word inside the half-year; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles. 'half' takes the back half of the word year.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarrying means lingering or staying on, waiting.
